findings.title: Event listener still runs V2 code when both FGAP features are enabled
findings.body: The new guard only checks ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ, but management() in this same class selects MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, regardless of the V1 flag. If both features are enabled, a ClientRemovedEvent therefore reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(), which unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, instead of the V2 case being skipped. The guard needs to exclude V2 (e.g. V1 && !V2) or the handler will throw on every client removal in that configuration.

findings.title: NullPointerException when the all-clients resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...), which can return null when the 'Clients' all-resource is absent from the store. The result is passed unchecked to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later dereferenced via resource.getScopes(), so a permission check crashes with an NPE/500 instead of returning false. The String-scope overload at lines 244-247 does null-check its resource; this overload needs the same guard.

findings.title: Existing FGAP V2 realms never receive the new Clients resource type
findings.body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, so realms that enabled FGAP V2 while the schema contained only Users will never get the new 'configure', 'map-roles-client-scope' and 'map-roles-composite' scopes nor the 'Clients' all-resource created later in this method. For those realms, creating Clients permissions fails with missing-scope errors and evaluation has no all-clients resource to fall back to. Initialization needs to be idempotent and add missing scopes/resources for existing clients, or a migration must create them.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the synthetic 'Clients' resource as a client id
findings.body: findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) also matches the all-clients resource, which AdminPermissionsSchema.init creates with both name and type set to 'Clients'. When an all-clients permission grants the scope, granted.add(resource.getName()) therefore inserts the literal string 'Clients' into a set whose contract is client ids. Callers filtering clients by id get a bogus entry, a non-empty check can pass while the set contains no real client, and an all-clients-only grant yields no actual client ids from this method. The resource-type resource must be skipped or expanded to the real clients it covers.

findings.title: canExchangeTo predicate now throws instead of returning a decision
findings.body: canExchangeTo is a boolean authorization predicate; before this change MgmtPermissionsV2 inherited the V1 ClientPermissions implementation and callers received true/false. Now that MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, every token-exchange permission check in a V2 deployment hits this unconditional UnsupportedOperationException, surfacing as a server error instead of a permit/deny decision and breaking client token exchange even for realms not using the new Clients permissions. The predicate should deny gracefully (or evaluate the applicable check) rather than throw.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type (returning 'All users' or the username) and falls through to resource.getDisplayName() for everything else. Client resources are created by getOrCreateResource with the client UUID as the resource name and no clientId-based display name, so permission and resource representations for the new Clients type expose a UUID, and the all-clients resource exposes 'Clients', instead of the clientId and an 'All clients' label analogous to Users. This makes the admin permission listings for clients misleading and inconsistent.
